claims.text: No. Per the PostgreSQL 17.0 docs, a regular CREATE INDEX can run in a transaction block, but CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot.

No. CONCURRENTLY avoids locking out writes, but it does not mean no waiting or zero impact. It needs two table scans and must wait for existing transactions that could modify or use the index, so it takes significantly longer and does more total work. The extra CPU and I/O can slow other operations. After the build finishes, the index may still be unusable for queries while transactions that predate the build exist. Before each scan the build waits for transactions that have modified the table. After the second scan it waits for transactions holding older snapshots. For partial indexes or indexes on expressions, this includes transactions in concurrent builds on other tables.

A failure while scanning the table, such as a deadlock or a uniqueness violation in a unique index, makes the command fail but leaves an INVALID index behind. Queries ignore it because it might be incomplete, but it still adds update overhead. psql \d shows it flagged INVALID. Expression or partial indexes can behave similarly if evaluating the expressions errors.

Yes, in both situations. For a unique index built concurrently, uniqueness is already enforced against other transactions when the second table scan begins. So constraint violations can be reported in other queries before the index is available for use, or even when the build eventually fails. If the failure happens in the second scan, the INVALID index keeps enforcing uniqueness afterwards.

Documented recovery, described only and not executed: identify the INVALID index, for example in psql \d output. The recommended method is to drop it and retry CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY. The docs also name REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY as another possibility. For a unique build that failed on a uniqueness violation, the supplied extract does not describe fixing the duplicate data, but the violation is stated as the failure cause. The invalid index may keep enforcing uniqueness until it is dropped (see C4).

No. Only one concurrent index build can run on a given table at a time. Regular (non-concurrent) builds can run simultaneously with each other on the same table. Schema modification of the table is not allowed during either kind of build. The extract does not say whether a concurrent build is blocked or errors when a second is attempted.

note.recommendation: Do not run CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside BEGIN/COMMIT, and run only one concurrent build per table. Plan for a longer build that waits on older transactions. After any failure, check for INVALID indexes. Use the documented fix: drop the invalid index and retry, or use REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY. Treat a leftover invalid unique index as still enforcing uniqueness, so it can reject writes until it is dropped or rebuilt. This is why it should be cleaned up promptly. Before retrying a unique build that failed on a violation, check the data for duplicates; this is my inference, not stated in the extract.
unknowns: Only the REL_17_0 create_index.sgml extract was available. Minor-release changes after 17.0 are unverified.
The extract does not say how to find invalid indexes by catalog query (for example pg_index.indisvalid); only psql \d is documented here.
The extract does not state what happens when a second concurrent build is started on the same table (wait or error).
The extract does not cover REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY details, the exact lock levels, or duplicate-data remediation.
